content.p: This Act may be cited as the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Cost Recovery) Act 2014.

Each provision of this Act specified in column 1 of the table commences, or is taken to have commenced, in accordance with column 2 of the table. Any other statement in column 2 has effect according to its terms.

The day this Act receives the Royal Assent.

content.p: Note: This table relates only to the provisions of this Act as originally enacted. It will not be amended to deal with any later amendments of this Act.
Any information in column 3 of the table is not part of this Act. Information may be inserted in this column, or information in it may be edited, in any published version of this Act.

Each Act that is specified in a Schedule to this Act is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this Act has effect according to its terms.

section.heading: Election to have an action management plan approved after approval of the taking of an action granted

content.p: A person proposing to take an action may, at any time before an approval of the taking of the action is granted under section 133, elect to submit an action management plan for approval.
An election must:
be in writing; and
be given to the Minister before the Minister grants an approval under section 133.

(3) If, after making an election, the person (the first person) notifies the Minister under section 156F that another person (the second person) proposes to take the action instead, the second person may revoke the election made by the first person under this section.
An election cannot be revoked once the Minister has granted an approval under section 133.

content.p: Before approving an action management plan, the Minister may publish:

If an action management plan is a condition of an approval of an action, the holder of the approval may, at any time, apply to the Minister for a variation of the action management plan.

Minister may approve a variation of action management plan
The Minister may approve a variation to an action management plan if requested to do so.

include the information (if any) prescribed by the regulations; and

content.p: Add:

The Minister may, in writing, determine the amounts of fees that may be charged if the approach for assessing the relevant impacts of an action that the Minister has decided is a controlled action is:
assessment by inquiry under Division 7 of Part 8; or
assessment by strategic assessment under Division 1 of Part 10.
Before making a determination, the Minister must consult:
the person proposing to take the action; or
if the person proposing to take the action is not the designated proponent—the designated proponent; or
if the approach is assessment by strategic assessment—the person responsible for the adoption or implementation of the relevant policy, plan or program;
about the amounts of fees to be charged.
The Minister may, in the determination made under subsection (1), determine the way in which a fee is to be worked out.
A determination made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.
Omit “environmental management plan”, substitute “action management plan”.
Insert:
This section applies if a fee is worked out by a person to whom a function or power is delegated under section 515.
If:
a method prescribed by the regulations under subsection 520(4C) has been used to work out a fee; and
the person required to pay the fee is dissatisfied with the way the method was used to work out the fee;
the person may apply to the Secretary for the Secretary to reconsider the way the method was used to work out the fee.
The application must:
be in a form prescribed by the regulations; and
set out the reasons for the application.
The application must be made within 30 business days after the applicant is informed of the fee.
A person may apply only once in relation to a fee.
Upon receiving an application for reconsideration of a fee, the Secretary must:
reconsider the way the method was used to work out the fee; and
either:
confirm the fee; or
work out a new fee by using the method again.
The person who undertakes the reconsideration must be:
the Secretary; or
an employee in the Department who:
was not involved in working out the fee; and
occupies a position that is senior to that occupied by any person involved in working out the fee.
The Secretary must give to the applicant a written notice that:
states the outcome of the reconsideration; and
gives reasons for that outcome.
The Secretary must undertake a reconsideration of a fee within 30 business days after receiving an application for reconsideration.
Insert:
The regulations may prescribe fees that are payable for services the Minister or Secretary provides in performing functions, or exercising powers, under this Act or the regulations.
A fee prescribed by the regulations is payable to the Commonwealth.
Regulations prescribing fees may also:
prescribe fees in respect of:
a particular class of decision; or
a particular class of action; or
a particular class of person; and
prescribe 2 or more fees for the same matter; and
prescribe a method for working out a fee; and
prescribe a method for working out the refund of part of a fee; and
(e) deal with other matters, including the following:
specifying the way in which, and times at which, a fee is to be paid;
specifying the fees that must be paid, and by whom, in the event of a transfer under section 145B or a change of person proposing to take an action under section 156F;
the consequences of failure to pay a specified fee;
the circumstances in which the Minister may waive a fee;
the circumstances in which a person is exempt from paying a specified fee;
the circumstances in which a fee may be refunded, in whole or in part.
Omit “Subsection (3) does”, substitute “Subsections (3), (4A) and (4C) do”.
Insert:

section.heading: Time does not run if all or part of fee remains unpaid

content.p: If:
one or more fees are payable in respect of a service the Minister or Secretary provides in performing functions, or exercising powers, under this Act or the regulations; and
a provision of this Act or the regulations:
requires or allows the Minister or Secretary to do a thing relating to the service; or
requires or allows the Minister or Secretary to do a thing relating to the service within a particular period; and
all of part of a fee relating to the service remains unpaid;
then:
if subparagraph (b)(i) applies—the Minister or Secretary need not do the thing until all of the required fee is paid; and
if subparagraph (b)(ii) applies and the period has not begun—the period does not begin until all of the required fee is paid; and
if subparagraph (b)(ii) applies and the period has begun—the period stops until all of the required fee is paid and, when paid, begins again for the balance of the period.
For the purposes of paragraphs (1)(e) and (f), the day that all of the required fee is paid is not to be counted in the relevant period.
Insert:

action management plan, in relation to an action, means a plan for managing the impacts of the action on a matter protected by a provision of Part 3, such as a plan for conserving habitat of a species.
Fees

The amendments made by items 2 to 5, 12, 13 and 15 to 19 of this Schedule apply in relation to a referral of a proposal to take an action that is received by the Minister on or after 14 May 2014 in respect of which a service is provided on or after the day this item commences.
Action management plans

The amendments made by items 1 and 19 of this Schedule apply in relation to a decision on the approach to be used for assessment of the relevant impacts of an action that is made on or after the day this item commences.
The amendments made by items 6 to 11, 14 and 19 of this Schedule apply in relation to an approval, whether granted before, on or after the day this item commences.
